PolSo virtual test campaign

Digital twin of the PM + gas source-attribution device (STM32 NUCLEO-G474RE, PMS7003, BME688, hooded PolSo-19 enclosure, 2000 mAh Li-ion), run before buying hardware. Generated 2026-10-11; 1,478 simulated sensor-hours, 11 min on this PC.

What this is and is not. Every number below comes from physics-based models whose parameters are literature/datasheet estimates (listed under Assumptions), not from PolSo hardware. The simulation is good at finding design problems (which conditions break the classifier, what the firmware must handle, whether the battery is big enough) and at comparing options. It cannot prove real-world accuracy: training and test data come from the same simulator, so real accuracy will be lower. Re-fit the assumptions with bench data from the first unit (see the last section).

Key findings

  1. Fusion is justified. On held-out field data the fused model reaches macro-F1 0.84 vs 0.76 (PM only) and 0.60 (gas only). PM alone separates dust from combustion; the BME688 heater profile is what separates vehicle, biomass and industrial combustion.
  2. A decision forest generalised better than the MLP on held-out field windows (macro-F1 0.95 vs 0.84). The deployed int8 MLP is tiny (1.8 KB); a pruned forest (e.g. 30 trees, depth 8, tens of KB) also fits the G474 and is worth comparing on real data.
  3. Chamber data alone will not generalise. A model trained only on chamber sessions scores macro-F1 0.68 outdoors vs 0.85 when diverse labelled field sessions (humidity, wind, background, ageing, several units) are added. Budget time for labelled field collection, not just chamber runs.
  4. Humidity is the biggest environmental risk. Accuracy by RH: 20% 94%, 40% 97%, 60% 95%, 75% 93%, 85% 83%, 92% 87%, 97% 76%. In fog, 0% of clean-air windows were blamed on a source (hygroscopic growth inflates PMS counts).
  5. The twin caught a firmware bug. The first gas-baseline tracker (rise 0.01 / fall 1e-4 per sample) slowly absorbed sustained pollution into the 'clean-air' baseline: on the 24 h test days accuracy fell from ~99 % in the first hours to 25-40 % by evening, and field-day selective accuracy was 73 %. Slower rates (0.0005 / 1e-6), chosen on separate development days (different seeds and unit), fixed it. Results below use the fixed firmware.
  6. Sensor drift needs on-device baseline tracking. macro-F1 at day 180: 0.82 with tracking vs 0.74 with the frozen factory baseline (day 365: 0.80 vs 0.63).
  7. Detection limit. Smallest excess PM2.5 attributed correctly 80 % of the time over a 30 ug/m3 background: biomass burning 50 ug/m3, dust 25 ug/m3, industrial 50 ug/m3, vehicle exhaust 100 ug/m3. Vehicle soot is mostly below the PMS7003 0.3 um cut, so traffic is recognised largely through gases.
  8. Unseen sources: cooking -> mostly 'biomass burning' (wrong 84%); dust storm -> mostly 'dust' (wrong 5%); fog -> mostly 'background' (wrong 0%); incense -> mostly 'biomass burning' (wrong 55%); trash burning -> mostly 'uncertain' (wrong 26%); two stroke traffic -> mostly 'uncertain' (wrong 16%). Cooking and incense have no class of their own, so expect them to be mislabelled unless a class is added.
  9. 24 h field days: selective accuracy 89% at 75% coverage (the device abstains on the rest).
  10. Firmware is small and fast. C core matches the Python twin on 100.00% of windows; 3.1 KB RAM, 1.8 KB model, ~0.18 ms per inference. The STM32G474 (128 KB SRAM, 512 KB flash) is far more than enough.
  11. Fan stall is invisible to the firmware. A slowed PMS fan still produces valid frames; the device kept reporting confident labels on 100% of windows afterwards. Dead sensors and UART corruption are handled (flagged / resynchronised).
  12. Power is the hard constraint. NUCLEO board, continuous: 7.3 h; Custom PCB, continuous: 11.0 h; Custom PCB, PMS 90 s on / 90 s off: 18.2 h; Custom PCB, PMS 90 s on / 270 s off: 27.2 h. The PMS7003 fan, the GPS and the NUCLEO's ST-LINK dominate.
  13. The confidence gate is the main accuracy/coverage dial. The deployed gate (0.95) was set on validation data to answer 90 % of clear windows. Several FAILs (T01, T02, T07) come mostly from abstentions being scored as errors. Trade-off on held-out data: gate 0.50: field sessions 96% correct @ 99% answered, 24 h days 82% @ 99%; gate 0.70: field sessions 97% correct @ 95% answered, 24 h days 85% @ 91%; gate 0.90: field sessions 98% correct @ 87% answered, 24 h days 88% @ 80%; gate 0.95: field sessions 98% correct @ 83% answered, 24 h days 89% @ 75%.

What to change before / while buying hardware

  1. Battery: 2000 mAh is not enough for all-day continuous use. Buy 2x 18650 cells in parallel (~6000-7000 mAh) or plan duty cycling; prefer a GPS with a power-save mode (u-blox M8/M10) over a NEO-6M.
  2. Prototype on the NUCLEO, deploy on a bare STM32G474 board (or cut the ST-LINK power): the debugger alone costs roughly 45 mA in this model, so measure it on day one.
  3. Configure the BME688 heater profile (10 steps, 150-400 C, parallel mode) - the static IAQ number is not enough; the per-step resistances are the fingerprint.
  4. Add a PMS fan-health check in firmware: flag when all count channels collapse together while gas and RH are steady, and periodically compare PM against the gas response; consider the PMS SET pin to power-cycle the sensor.
  5. Revisit the 80 % data-validity rule: with 30 % of PMS frames lost (loose wire, noisy UART) the device went silent on 92% of windows even though the remaining frames were good. Use short, shielded UART leads, and consider accepting windows with >= 50 % valid frames.
  6. Handle humidity explicitly: keep the separate BME688 vent, log RH with every window, and treat RH > 90 % as low-confidence (or add a small inlet heater / RH correction once real PM-vs-RH data is collected).
  7. Keep the hooded inlet from PolSo-19 and print it first; verify inlet loss with a fan test (the model assumes PolSo-19 coefficients).
  8. Data plan: chamber runs for each source + at least several days of labelled field data per class across humidity/seasons, with 3+ different units, logged at 1 Hz raw (counts + per-step resistance) - not just PM/IAQ outputs.
  9. First week with hardware: (1) measure each rail's current; (2) 48 h co-location of all units in clean air to fit unit spread and noise; (3) RH step test; (4) a few chamber exposures (incense/candle, road dust, vehicle exhaust); then re-fit params.py and re-run this campaign before building all 10 units.

How the sources look to the sensors

Mean features from chamber tests on the 10 unseen pilot units. Dust shows up in the coarse bins; combustion sources separate mainly through the gas heater profile (NO2 from diesel raises resistance at 200 C, VOCs lower it at 250-300 C).

Test details

T00 - Generalisation to unseen field sessions + unseen units PASS

Criterion: chamber+field model macro-F1 >= 0.85 on held-out field data

Chamber+field model: macro-F1 0.85, coverage 83%, selective accuracy 98%. Chamber-only model: macro-F1 0.68, selective accuracy 76%. int8 quantisation cost +0.3 pts accuracy.

T01 - Chamber tests, single sources (in-distribution) FAIL

Criterion: macro-F1 >= 0.90

macro-F1 0.90, coverage 84%, selective accuracy 99% over 2201 windows on the 10 unseen pilot units.

T02 - Detection limit (excess PM2.5 over a 30 ug/m3 background) FAIL

Criterion: >= 80 % correct attribution at <= 50 ug/m3 excess for every class

Smallest excess PM2.5 (ug/m3) attributed correctly >= 80 % of the time: biomass burning 50, dust 25, industrial 50, vehicle exhaust 100.

T03 - Humidity sweep 20-97 % RH (incl. fog) FAIL

Criterion: accuracy drop at 85 % RH <= 10 pts vs 40-60 % RH; false source alarms in fog <= 10 %

Accuracy by RH: 20% 94%, 40% 97%, 60% 95%, 75% 93%, 85% 83%, 92% 87%, 97% 76%. Drop at 85 % RH: 13 pts. Fog (RH>=92 %, no source): 0% of windows falsely blamed on a source.

T04 - Temperature sweep 5-45 C PASS

Criterion: accuracy spread across temperatures <= 10 pts

Accuracy by temperature: 5 C 95%, 15 C 92%, 25 C 95%, 35 C 93%, 45 C 89% (spread 6 pts).

T05 - Wind speed x direction x inlet design (PolSo-19 enclosures) PASS

Criterion: hooded design: accuracy drop at 4 m/s <= 5 pts vs calm

Accuracy at 0.3 / 2 / 4 / 6 m/s - baseline: 93% / 96% / 91% / 88%; hooded: 94% / 93% / 94% / 88%; multi_hole: 96% / 92% / 90% / 89%. PM10 bias at 4 m/s for dust (0/90/180 deg): baseline -3%/-9%/-18%; hooded -1%/-2%/-4%; multi_hole -9%/-8%/-9%. Model trained on hooded-enclosure data only.

T06 - Mixed sources (50/50 and 75/25 pairs) PASS

Criterion: answered label is a real contributor >= 85 %; dominant source found >= 70 % at 75/25

Answered labels naming a real contributor: 100%. Abstained on 40% of mixed windows. Dominant source correctly named at 75/25: 71%.

T07 - Response time to a new source FAIL

Criterion: median time-to-correct-label <= 90 s and <= 10 % never detected

Median 149 s, 90th percentile 230 s from source onset to first correct label (60 s window, 30 s hop, EMA smoothing); 2% never detected.

T08 - Sensor ageing / drift 0-365 days PASS

Criterion: macro-F1 drop at 180 days <= 10 pts with on-device baseline tracking

macro-F1 with baseline tracking: day 0 0.81, day 30 0.82, day 90 0.82, day 180 0.82, day 365 0.80. With frozen factory baseline: day 0 0.83, day 30 0.82, day 90 0.80, day 180 0.74, day 365 0.63.

T09 - Unit-to-unit variation (10 pilot prototypes) PASS

Criterion: std of macro-F1 across units <= 0.05 and worst unit >= 0.80

macro-F1 mean 0.88, std 0.023, worst unit 0.83, best 0.91 (same scenarios replayed on every unit).

T10 - Unseen source subtypes and confounders FAIL

Criterion: confident-wrong <= 25 % on unseen subtypes and <= 30 % on confounders (cooking, incense); fog <= 10 %

cooking: correct 0% / uncertain 16% / wrong 84%; dust_storm: correct 83% / uncertain 12% / wrong 5%; fog: correct 100% / uncertain 0% / wrong 0%; incense: correct 0% / uncertain 45% / wrong 55%; trash_burning: correct 22% / uncertain 52% / wrong 26%; two_stroke_traffic: correct 28% / uncertain 56% / wrong 16%.

T11 - 24-hour field days in six environments PASS

Criterion: overall selective accuracy >= 80 % at coverage >= 70 %

All days: selective accuracy 89%, coverage 75%, macro-F1 0.77. Construction site, pre-monsoon summer: 99% @ 94%; Highway toll plaza: 45% @ 54%; Industrial estate: 100% @ 72%; Residential park, monsoon: 100% @ 89%; Rural village, crop-burning season: 100% @ 88%; Urban roadside, winter (Delhi-like): 58% @ 51%.

T12 - Fault injection (UART, sensor death, fan stall, I2C, SD card) FAIL

Criterion: no crashes; dead sensors flagged >= 95 %; 0.1 % UART errors cost <= 3 pts; stalled-fan windows not reported as a confident source (<= 5 %)

none: acc 92%, flagged-after 0%, confident-after 79%; uart_bit_errors_0.1%: acc 93%, flagged-after 0%, confident-after 79%; uart_bit_errors_1%+slips: acc 100%, flagged-after 92%, confident-after 8%; pms_frames_dropped_30%: acc 100%, flagged-after 92%, confident-after 7%; pms_dead_after_1h: acc 99%, flagged-after 100%, confident-after 0%; pms_fan_stall_after_1h: acc 93%, flagged-after 0%, confident-after 100%; bme_i2c_errors_40%: acc 100%, flagged-after 96%, confident-after 4%; bme_dead_after_1h: acc 99%, flagged-after 100%, confident-after 0%; sd_write_fail_20%: acc 92%, flagged-after 0%, confident-after 79%. No crashes.

T13 - Firmware C vs Python twin (software-in-the-loop) PASS

Criterion: label agreement >= 99.5 %, max probability diff <= 0.01, RAM <= 32 KB, inference <= 10 ms

Labels agree on 100.00% of 537 windows (incl. a stream with UART corruption and I2C errors); max probability difference 1.1e-07; max relative feature difference 1.8e-03. Firmware state 3.1 KB RAM, model 1.8 KB flash, 1392 MACs per inference, est. ~0.18 ms per window at 170 MHz (measure with the DWT cycle counter on the board). Builds with -Wall -Wextra and no warnings.

T14 - Battery life (2000 mAh Li-ion) and duty cycling FAIL

Criterion: >= 24 h continuous sampling in the configuration as specified (NUCLEO + 2000 mAh)

NUCLEO board, continuous: 7.3 h (232 mA avg); Custom PCB, continuous: 11.0 h (154 mA avg); Custom PCB, PMS 90 s on / 90 s off: 18.2 h (93 mA avg); Custom PCB, PMS 90 s on / 270 s off: 27.2 h (63 mA avg). Duty cycling keeps selective accuracy at 85% (1/2 duty) and 85% (1/4 duty) but only samples 33% / 17% of the time, so short events are missed.

T15 - Research question: PM-only vs gas-only vs fused PASS

Criterion: fused macro-F1 >= best single-sensor model + 0.05

macro-F1 (no abstention) on all held-out field windows: PM-only 0.76, gas-only 0.60, fused MLP 0.84 (+0.09), fused random forest 0.95.

Assumptions (re-fit these with real data)

ItemValue usedBasis / how to measure
PMS7003 detection efficiency50 % at 0.45 um, falls to 50 % again at 3.5 umLow-cost OPC evaluations; measure vs a reference OPC/APS in a chamber
PMS7003 sizing blur / counting volumesigma 0.3 (ln), 2.0 cm3/sFit from 1 Hz count noise in clean air
PMS7003 unit gain spread10% (lognormal)Co-locate the 10 units for 48 h
Hygroscopic growth (kappa)soot 0.05, smoke 0.15-0.2, sulfate-rich 0.35-0.45, dust 0.03Petters & Kreidenweis 2007; check PM vs RH against a dried reference
BME688 gas sensitivitiesGaussian in heater T; CO@340 C, NO2@190 C (oxidising), oVOC@270 C, aromatics@360 CBosch BME AI-Studio sessions with known gases
BME688 humidity coefficient0.035 -> 0.027 ln(R) per g/m3 (150 -> 400 C)Humidity steps in clean air
BME688 unit spreadR0 0.35, sensitivity 0.15 (lognormal sigma)Per-unit zero-air calibration
BME688 drift0.002 ln/day + random walk 0.01/sqrt(day)Long-term co-location
Emission ratiose.g. diesel CO 25 / NO2 2.5 ppb per ug/m3; biomass CO 6-10, oVOC 0.8-1.5Akagi 2011; roadside studies
Inlet lossesPolSo-19 Run A (hooded coarse loss 4.4 % mean at 4 m/s)Wind-tunnel / fan test of the printed hood
Power drawPMS 80 mA@5 V, BME 9 mA, MCU 6-30 mA, NUCLEO overhead 45 mA, GPS 45 mAMeasure each rail with a USB power meter / INA219
Firmware60 s window, 30 s hop, 300 s warm-up, EMA 0.5Design choice

Reproduce

cd simulation → python run_all.py (full, ~11 min) or python run_all.py --quick. Unit tests: python -m unittest discover tests. Firmware core: firmware_c/ (portable C99, drop into STM32CubeIDE; model_params.h is generated).
